$comment: Glossary for L-13 (doc 06 §3.7, §4.3; doc 08 §7.2; R64). Sources: doc 08 §7.2.1 tables T-A–T-E (it column), each value checked against WordByWordPrototype/Localizable.xcstrings (localizations.it) and the app's Free/Plus comparison labels (FeatureQuotaManager.swift featureDisplayName); §7.2.2 rules ①–③ (no X-fix lists it); §7.3 it row (tu; 'scorri verso destra', 'tocca due volte').

required: kickers and quota-table rows use the app's names (rule ①). Kickers drop the '(Significato AI)' suffix like en / ja / es / fr; quota rows are shortened so each fits the 390 px table in two lines (engine as '· cloud' / '· locale', the lookup row as '(AI)'), as es does. 'Scorri per Tradurre' keeps the app's capital T (the kicker is upper-cased by CSS; reported to the app side). Action Flow keeps the App Store name in headings and the sample (doc 08 D3, §7.2.3); the quota row uses the app's own comparison label 'Flusso azioni della frase' (sentence_skeleton_settings_navigation_title), as zh-Hans / ko / es do.

Rule ③ correction: the app's pronunciation labels read 'AI Pronuncia (Parola)' / 'AI Pronuncia (Frase)' (English word order); the website writes 'Pronuncia AI · parola / frase' and reports the string to the app side.

AI, not IA: every Italian app string writes 'AI' (Lettura AI, Significato AI, Ottieni spiegazione sintattica AI, AI Pronuncia, voce AI); the website follows the app so quoted names and sentences match (deviation from the '(IA)' in doc 03 §2.3 table A / doc 08 §7.3 — owner decision recorded in docs/redesign-2026/ops/m3/it-qa.md).

contains: app button and screen names the sentences quote verbatim in “ ” (rule ①; T-B get_syntax_explanation_button, view_title_swipe_history; T-C audio_playback_title_*; T-E upgrade_now_button / restore_purchase_button). The app's straight apostrophe is set as ’ on the website.
banned: left swipes (F14); mouse wording (X7 by analogy); a single tap for lookup (doc 08 §1.1); variants of the app names; 'IA' (see above).

banned.note: the gesture is a right swipe; a left swipe removes the translation (F14)
touch gesture, not a mouse double-click (doc 08 §7.2.2 X7 by analogy)
lookup is a double tap, never a single tap (doc 08 §1.1 lookup row)
the app's ai_pronunciation_* labels use English word order (rule ③; reported to the app side)
the Italian app writes AI everywhere; the website follows it (owner decision, it-qa.md)
